D1.option: Authenticate canonical genesis in circuit over committed state, binding the program, input, initial fuel and stack limit, and require a genesis-start segment before sealing any GP-1 outcome. This addresses the supplied-digest check at crates/mori-recursion/src/ivc.rs:498–501 and tools/sherlock-sdk/sherlock-run.compact:29–35; the initialization parameters are confirmed at crates/mori-core/src/sherlock/reference.rs:14–25.
D1.kill_criterion: Reopen the placement of initialization if establishing canonical program/input state requires work that cannot fit one leaf; use authenticated initialization continuations instead. Cost alone must not reverse the requirement for authenticated genesis.
D1.first_experiment: Proposed: derive a field-by-field mapping from the reference constructor to committed-state Init, preserving u128 fuel, both fuel registers, empty environment/frame semantics and Pending outcome. Compare literal, add and fact(3), then measure the implemented check and test forged entry metadata, fuel, stack limit and non-genesis sealing. No experiment was run in this review.

D2.option: Prototype a separate, fixed-key, single-phase Halo2 chiplet leaf U: processor registers route requests to program, write-once memory/linked-stack, u128 arithmetic and hash tables through native lookup arguments, with all chips inside one proof and authenticated state commitments across segments. Start with T=16 owner steps and target k_U<=19; k_U=17 and 5–9 seconds per leaf, or 0.31–0.56 seconds per owner step, remain ESTIMATE hypotheses rather than established costs.

findings.problem: The proposed implementation boundary is incomplete. An ordinary Relation cannot install arbitrary chiplet gates or lookup_any arguments: its circuit configuration comes from ZkStdLib. Cand-0c40 also cites nonexistent vendored circuits/stdlib 0.8.3 sources. A custom LogUp bus is not supported merely because the underlying prover supports lookups.
findings.next_action: Implement U as a custom Halo2 Circuit using the pinned gadgets, with an explicit fixed constraint system verified by R, or specify the required stdlib extension. Use native single-phase lookups initially; adopting LogUp requires a separately specified challenge schedule and recursive-verifier extension.
findings.evidence: The workspace pins midnight-proofs 0.8.3, midnight-circuits 7.3.0 and midnight-zk-stdlib 2.4.0. Relation exposes circuit and used_chips, while MidnightCircuit delegates configuration to ZkStdLib. Native lookup_any exists at tools/profile/vendor/midnight-proofs-0.8.3/src/plonk/circuit.rs:1889–1913; the recursive verifier asserts one phase at midnight-circuits-7.3.0/src/verifier/verifier_gadget.rs:308–310 and handles native lookups at :318–336.

findings.location: cand-f429 D2 bus; cand-0c40 D2 memory chiplet; tools/profile/vendor/midnight-proofs-0.8.3/src/plonk/lookup.rs:42–67
findings.problem: Set inclusion does not establish address uniqueness, allocation freshness, read-after-write ordering or memory boundary consistency. A valid dictionary lookup can still return a future write or one of two conflicting values unless those properties are constrained. The proposals do not yet provide that relation.

Re-encode frame/task rewrites as persistent linked entries, and test conflicting duplicate addresses, reads before allocation, omitted writes and substituted roots. Keep program contents in authenticated witness data rather than program-specific fixed columns.

Runtime data/environment/value-slot tables append at crates/mori-core/src/sherlock/helper_machine/shared/owner_runtime.rs:3513–3564, but task and frame tops are rewritten and popped at :3566–3588. These operations need the proposed representation refinement.

findings.problem: G-C is not demonstrated. With one R per U, 19 leaves require 19 R proofs and 18 N merges, plus C and D; cand-0c40 counts that alternative as 19 recursive steps. Leaf-worker overlap, lift cost and memory also remain unmeasured.

SRC-011 explicitly gives unbuilt or unmeasured improvements no G-C credit. Both benchmarks require actual receipts below 7,200 seconds, 48 GB per process and 100 GB aggregate.

D2.kill_criterion: Reject this realization if its authenticated lookup/memory relation is unsound, if useful owner-step throughput cannot fit the supported leaf domain, or if the complete U/R/N/C/D pipeline fails G-C. Reduce segment size or redesign the bus before considering a different inner proof system; per-rule keys over the existing oversized facts block are not a demonstrated fallback.
D2.first_experiment: Proposed: first specify and inspect the custom Circuit-to-R interface and write-once memory invariants. Then model a minimal native-lookup leaf with authenticated old-cell reads, fresh writes, a stack rewrite and one arithmetic operation; include its actual verifier in R before extrapolating to T=16.

D3.option: (i) Recommend the explicit binary-composition OWNER AMENDMENT below for the separate-leaf design, while retaining literal GP-4 until it is adopted; (ii) use authenticated adapters with a uniform outer interface and preserve a path for non-stdlib constraint systems and other SRS identities. (iii) Require verification of supplied ledger proofs with the keyed Blake2b-512 transcript, and (iv) use expandable commitments with authenticated continuations rather than introducing a 32- or 64-bit storage ceiling.

findings.problem: Two slots holding prior proofs cannot also hold a separate new-work proof. Counting routine join/seal bookkeeping as sufficient new work is not established by the proposal. Cand-fd2b correctly identifies binary nesting as an amendment rather than claiming existing compliance.

chiplets_assessment: The owner's direction addresses the measured duplication of program walks, value scans and range checks. Specialised regions within one proof are an established chiplet pattern, as documented in the [Miden chiplet implementation](https://docs.rs/miden-vm/latest/miden_vm/trace/chiplets/struct.Chiplets.html), but its performance does not transfer to this stack. The best initial realization here uses native single-phase Halo2 lookups with explicit dictionary and memory invariants, keeping all chiplets in U and linking segments through authenticated state and continuation commitments. Separate chip proofs would require an additional cross-proof bus protocol; matching bus digests alone would not establish request/response consistency. Chiplets do not by themselves decide whether U should ultimately remain separate from N.
proposed_requirement_text: WHEN a run is introduced at genesis, its proof SHALL authenticate the canonical initial state from the committed program, machine version, input and execution parameters, preserving the specified fuel width and initialization semantics; equality with a caller-supplied init_d SHALL NOT suffice.

WHEN a segment is sealed as a run claim, the sealing relation SHALL establish authenticated genesis, no pending initialization or memory operation, and a terminal outcome of Halted(v), Rejected(code) or Exhausted(kind), with canonical outcome encoding and authenticated dependencies.

WHEN the processor issues a chiplet request, the leaf SHALL constrain its operation, operands, result, table identity and activation; memory requests SHALL additionally establish unique address bindings, allocation validity, read timing and consistency with authenticated segment boundaries.

WHEN an authenticated-memory operation exceeds one segment's work capacity, the proof SHALL carry its complete continuation state under the same key; continuation work SHALL preserve owner-step and fuel semantics, SHALL make authenticated progress, and SHALL NOT impose a new fixed storage-capacity ceiling.

WHEN a foreign circuit is admitted, the proof SHALL authenticate the foreign key and adapter identity, including the constraint system, degree, exact instance layout, transcript, format and SRS; an incompatible SRS obligation SHALL be discharged under its own parameters before entering the common accumulator.

WHEN a claim states that supplied ledger proof bytes were verified, its adapter SHALL enforce the pinned keyed Blake2b-512 transcript, canonical encodings, required point checks and complete parsing; Poseidon re-proving SHALL NOT satisfy that claim or close the final GP-3 acceptance gate.

WHEN a node selects a named verification key, the same constrained selector SHALL select the permitted statement type and every deferred fixed-base coefficient destination; closure SHALL pin all named keys and discharge every carried obligation.

WHEN G-C is evaluated, the measurement SHALL include every leaf, lift, merge, closing and decider proof, setup, independent verification and call validation, with measured contention and both memory peaks; estimates SHALL NOT constitute a passing result.

OWNER AMENDMENT — GP-4, proposed and not effective unless adopted: WHEN a node combines proofs, it SHALL accept at least two proof slots, each containing a prior-node proof or newly proved work; combining two prior proofs with additional proved work MAY use multiple nodes under the same fixed key set. Chain, tree and DAG support, shape binding, constant final proof size and depth-independent verification cost SHALL remain required.
